'''Damjan Rudež''' (born 17 June 1986) is a Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player. He represented the [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national team]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=10}},<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/rudezda01.html|title=Damjan Rudež Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=4 July 2020}}</ref> he played at both forward positions.

==Professional career==
===Europe===
From 2002 to 2004, Rudež played for the junior team of [[KK Zrinjevac|Zrinjevac]] and occasionally for the senior team. From 2004 to 2006, he played for the Belgian club [[BC Oostende|Oostende]], where he won his first championship in 2006. From 2006 to 2008, he played for [[KK Split|Split]].

In June 2008, he signed a two-year deal with [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija]]. In 2009, he left Olimpija and signed with [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]].

On 7 July 2011, he signed a one-year deal with [[KK Cibona|Cibona Zagreb]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cups/adriatic-league/87153/kk-cibona-lands-rudez-and-kovacevic.html | title=KK Cibona lands Rudez and Kovacevic | date=7 July 2011 | publisher=Sportando | access-date=9 August 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In August 2012, he signed a one-year deal with [[Basket Zaragoza 2002|CAI Zaragoza]] of Spain.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/94589/cai-zaragoza-puts-damjan-rudez-at-forward.html CAI Zaragoza puts Damjan Rudez at forward]</ref> On 26 June 2013, he re-signed with Zaragoza on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/114482/8174/cai-zaragoza-re-signs-rudez |title=CAI ZARAGOZA re-signs Rudez |access-date=2 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714163148/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/114482/8174/cai-zaragoza-re-signs-rudez |archive-date=14 July 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/102472/cai-zaragoza-keep-damjan-rudez.html CAI Zaragoza keep Damjan Rudez]</ref> In June 2014, he requested a buy-out from his contract with Zaragoza.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/121441/damjan-rudez-to-workout-with-cleveland-cavaliers.html Damjan Rudez to workout with Cleveland Cavaliers]</ref>

===NBA===
On 11 July 2014, Rudež signed a three-year deal with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-announce-three-player-signings Pacer Sign Free Agents C.J. Miles and Damjan Rudez; Re-sign Lavoy Allen]</ref><ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--pacers-reach-agreement-with-european-shooter-damjan-rudez-143317388.html Sources: Pacers reach agreement with European shooter Damjan Rudez]</ref> During [[2014–15 NBA season]], Rudež led all rookies in three-point field goal percentage.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player NBA Player 3-Point Shooting Statistics - 2014-15]</ref>

On 12 July 2015, Rudež was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Chase Budinger]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Acquire Damjan Rudez from Indiana|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-acquire-damjan-rudez-indiana|work=NBA.com|date=12 July 2015|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> On 27 June 2016, the Timberwolves declined the $1.2 million team option on Rudež's contract for the 2016–17 season, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gauruder|first=Dana|title=Timberwolves Decline Option On Damjan Rudez|url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2016/06/timberwolves-decline-option-on-damjan-rudez.html|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=27 June 2016|access-date=4 August 2016}}</ref>

On 8 September 2016, Rudež signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-six-free-agents-training-camp-nick-johnson-cliff-alexander-damjan-rudez-20160908|title=Orlando Magic Sign Six Players|work=NBA.com|date=8 September 2016|access-date=8 September 2016}}</ref> On 7 September 2017, he re-signed with the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-re-sign-damjan-rudez|title=Magic Re-Sign Damjan Rudez|work=NBA.com|date=7 September 2017|access-date=7 September 2017}}</ref> On 13 October 2017, he was waived by the Magic.<ref>{{cite news|title=Magic Waive Kalin Lucas and Damjan Rudez|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-kalin-lucas-and-damjan-rudez|access-date=14 October 2017|work=NBA.com|date=13 October 2017}}</ref>

===Return to Europe===
On 26 October 2017, Rudež signed a three-month contract with Spanish club [[Valencia Basket]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Valencia adds versatile forward Rudez|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8agmv69gucyjvhcg/valencia-adds-versatile-forward-rudez|access-date=26 October 2017|work=Euroleague.net|date=26 October 2017}}</ref> Following the expiration of his contract, on 29 January 2018, he parted ways with Valencia.<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/spain/acb/262946/damjan-rudez-leaves-valencia.html Damjan Rudez leaves Valencia]</ref> On 16 July 2018, Rudež signed a one-year contract with Spanish club [[CB Murcia|UCAM Murcia]].<ref>{{cite news |title=ACB.COM - Damjan Rudez, nuevo soldado de los Tercios del UCAM Murcia CB |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=142182 |access-date=16 July 2018 |work=www.acb.com |date=16 July 2018 |language=es-ES |archive-date=16 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180716194908/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=142182 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
Eventough he had several offers, Rudež made the choice to stay home during the 2019–2020 season to take care of his baby. He planned to return in March, April or May, but the coronavirus made a return impossible.<ref>{{cite news |title=youtube.com - Damjan Rudež, welkom bij Donar! 270620 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KEj3v-dB04Q  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/KEj3v-dB04Q |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|access-date=28 June 2020 |work=www.youtube.com |date=27 June 2020 |language=nl-NL}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

On 27 June 2020, Rudež signed with [[Donar Groningen|Donar]] in the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.donar.nl/nieuws/donar-versterkt-zich-met-damjan-rudez/|title=Donar versterkt zich met Damjan Rudež|access-date=27 June 2020}}</ref> His brother [[Ivan Rudež|Ivan]] had signed before as head coach. He averaged 7.9 points, 4 rebounds and 3 assists in the [[Dutch Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Damjan Rudez, Basketball Player |url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/18935/damjan-rudez |website=Proballers |access-date=13 September 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

In November, 2021, Rudež announced his retirement from playing basketball and his intention to remain professionally in the sport.<ref>{{cite news |title=HRVAT KOJI JE ZA JEDAN SAT OČARAO LARRYJA BIRDA: 'PRIŠAO MI JE I REKAO: NE IDEŠ NIGDJE, POTPISUJEŠ ZA NAS' |trans-title=The Croat who fascinated Larry Bird in one hour: 'He approached me and said: you're not going anywhere, you're signing for us'|url=https://sportske.jutarnji.hr/sn/kosarka/kosarka-mix/hrvat-koji-je-za-jedan-sat-ocarao-larryja-birda-prisao-mi-je-i-rekao-ne-ides-nigdje-potpisujes-za-nas-15119101 |access-date=12 November 2021 |work=sportske.jutarnji.hr |date=11 November 2021 |language=hr}}</ref>

==National team career==
On 3 August 2008, he was called into the senior [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national basketball team]] to compete at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]], after [[Damir Markota]] withdrew from the team, due to injury.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080810024726/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olym/men/news/lateNews/p/newsid/27516/FE_news_lateNews_arti.html CRO – Rudez called by Croatia after meniscus injury knocks out Markota]</ref>

In 2009, he won the gold medal at the [[Basketball at the 2009 Mediterranean Games|XVI Mediterranean Games]], which were held in Pescara, Italy. He also represented Croatia at the [[EuroBasket 2015]],<ref>{{cite news|title=CROATIA UNVEIL AMBITIOUS EUROBASKET SQUAD|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|access-date=13 September 2015|work=eurobasket2015.org|date=4 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913045910/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=13 September 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref> where they were eliminated in the eighth-finals by the [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CZECHS MAKE FIRST QUARTER-FINAL TRIP|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|access-date=13 September 2015|work=eurobasket2015.org|date=13 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914214822/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=14 September 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref>
